title: Cliques in the Ellington band? Observing before talking
summary: Outsiders told him the band had cliques; he joked he must belong to all of them and says you only know people by working with them.

story.theme_name: Duke Ellington and his orchestra, as others knew them
story.community_name: Duke Ellington: the band, the man, his men

blocks.x: That was such a big band. Was there much unity in the band or were there little cliques and saxophone players stick together and trumpet players stick together?

Well, there's a sort of a little joke about that, because, as I say, people on the outside didn't know what went on on the inside of the band. So the musicians who weren't in the band, you know, all of the musicians about town, they'd say to me, 'Well, how are you getting along?'

Then they'd say, "They tell me that they have cliques in the band." So I'd say, "Cliques? Well, if they have cliques in the band I must belong to all of them, because I don't know anything about it." Which I didn't. But you must realize that I've known these fellows.
And they knew me, see? And this period when I told you, I didn't -- I had practically nothing at all to say when I was riding the bus, because I was sort of learning the fellows.
Because you never really know a man till you work with him or live with him. That's how you get to know a man. So that's what it was.
